caption: Behaviors evaluated in dogs to assess age-related cognitive decline.
rows: Goes to wrong side of doors (e.g., hinge side)
Gets stuck and cannot navigate around or over obstacles
Decreased recognition of familiar people, pets or places
Decreased interest in petting or contact
Alterations or problems with social hierarchy
In need of constant contact (e.g., over dependent or "clingy")
Decreased daytime sleep/increased wandering or pacing
Staring, fixation or snapping at objects
Increased interest (volume eaten or speed of eating)
May seem to have a decline in vision, hearing or odor perception
Restless sleep or awake at night
a) House soiling: Indoor elimination at random sites or in view of owners
Goes outdoors, eliminates indoors upon return
Elimination in crate or sleeping area
Impaired responsiveness to known commands or tricks
Inability or slow to learn new tasks (must retrain)
note: 表内为单栏列表（无表头行，原文用加粗编号小标题分组）；表末脚注：*Adapted with permission from Landsberg G, Hunthausen W, Ackerman L. The effects of aging on behavior in senior pets. Handbook of Behavior Problems of the Dog and Cat. Edinburgh, Scotland: Elsevier Health Sciences, 2003.
